fi-paracheirodon-axelrodi.title: Cardinal Tetra
fi-paracheirodon-axelrodi.summary: A brilliant red-and-blue schooling tetra for warm, soft-water community and planted tanks.
rows: Schooling. Keep a group of at least 8–10
Omnivore. Quality flakes or micro-pellets plus live or frozen bloodworm, daphnia and similar small foods
Easy for farm-bred fish. Wild fish are less forgiving of poor water
Rio Negro and Orinoco basins (Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela). Most are now farm-bred
notes: Looks best in a planted tank with fairly dim light, driftwood and some floating plants.
Good tankmates: other small tetras, pencilfish, hatchetfish, small catfish and peaceful dwarf cichlids.

fi-paracheirodon-innesi.title: Neon Tetra
fi-paracheirodon-innesi.summary: The neon tetra, Paracheirodon innesi, is a small characid from the Amazon basin in Colombia, Brazil and Peru, found in acidic forest streams. Years of commercial breeding have weakened the ornamental…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
The type locality was originally given as 'near Iquitos', referring to the city of that name in the rainforest of Loreto region, Peru, although the specimens themselves derived…
notes: Provided healthy stock can be obtained (see 'Notes') maintenance presents few problems although it perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-phenacogrammus-interruptus.title: Congo Tetra
fi-phenacogrammus-interruptus.summary: The Congo tetra, Phenacogrammus interruptus, is a tetra from parts of the River Congo drainage in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Wild populations are endemic there, but most fish in the trade are…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Omnivore. An omnivore feeding on small worms, insects, crustaceans , algae and other zooplankton in nature.
Wild populations are endemic to parts of the River Congo drainage in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
notes: Ideally an African biotope tank with driftwood branches, floating vegetation and anubias.
However they will show their best colours in any well-planted setup with plenty of swimming space.

fi-hyphessobrycon-herbertaxelrodi.title: Black Neon Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-herbertaxelrodi.summary: The black neon tetra, Hyphessobrycon herbertaxelrodi, is a characid from the upper rio Paraguai in Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. A ubiquitous aquarium fish since its discovery, it is…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you will be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
This species appears to be widespread throughout the upper rio Paraguai in the states of Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, both north and south of the the vast tropical…
notes: Perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches, or heavily-planted planted set-up.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-hasemania-nana.title: Silver-tipped Tetra
fi-hasemania-nana.summary: The silvertip tetra, Hasemania nana, is a characid from the Rio São Francisco basin in Brazil. It inhabits creeks and tributaries away from the main river channels. Hasemania is one of the few…
notes: Adaptable and will do well in most types of setup, but is particularly well-suited to a heavily planted tank.
Oddly enough, aquatic plants are not a feature of its natural environment.

fi-hyphessobrycon-megalopterus.title: Black Phantom Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-megalopterus.summary: The black phantom tetra, Megalamphodus megalopterus, is a characid from the upper rio Madeira and upper rio Paraguai in Bolivia and Brazil. Most records are from the rio Guaporé (Río Iténez in…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens since this species forms temporary dominance hierarchies within which males compete for female attention, and therefore displays more interesting behaviour and better colouration when maintained in numbers.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
Native to the upper rio Madeira , a major branch of the western Amazon watershed in Bolivia and western Brazil , including its major tributaries the rios Beni and Mamoré , plus…
notes: Perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches, or heavily-planted planted set-up.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-hyphessobrycon-robertsi.title: Roberts Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-robertsi.summary: The ornate tetra, Megalamphodus bentosi, is a small characid whose type locality lies on the main channel of the lower Amazon at Óbidos, Brazil. It is very similar to a number of congeners, some of…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens since this species forms temporary dominance hierarchies within which males compete for female attention, and therefore displays more interesting behaviour and better colouration when maintained in numbers.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
Type locality is ' Amazon River at Obidos, Pará, Brazil ', which corresponds to the municipality of Óbidos in the lower Amazon basin, located on the river's main channel between…
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with live plants and a dark substrate.
A natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots are formed.

fi-hyphessobrycon-rosaceus.title: Rosy Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-rosaceus.summary: The rosy tetra, Megalamphodus rosaceus, is a small characid from Guyana, Suriname and Brazil, in river systems including the Essequibo and Corantijn. It is so similar to Megalamphodus bentosi that it…
rows: group of at least 6 of these, preferably 10 or more.
Feeds chiefly on small invertebrates in nature.
notes: A biotope setup would be very simple to arrange.

Use a substrate of river sand and add a few driftwood branches (if you can't find driftwood of the desired shape, common beech is safe to use if thoroughly dried and stripped of bark) and twisted roots.

fi-gymnocorymbus-ternetzi.title: Black Skirt Tetra
fi-gymnocorymbus-ternetzi.summary: The black widow tetra, Gymnocorymbus ternetzi, is a characid from the Rio Paraguay and Guaporé basins in Brazil, Bolivia and Argentina. All the fish in the trade are captive bred and unfussy about…
rows: Omnivore. A most unfussy, omnivorous species.
Rio Paraguay and Guaporé basins in Brazil , Bolivia and Argentina .
notes: It's an active species and prefers plenty of open swimming space, along with some quieter areas.

fi-pristella-maxillaris.title: Pristella maxillaris
fi-pristella-maxillaris.summary: The X-ray tetra, Pristella maxillaris, is a small characid native to coastal waters of Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana and northern Brazil. In the dry season it lives in clearwater…
rows: group of at least 6 of these, preferably 10 or more.
Carnivore / micropredator. A micropredator , it feeds mainly on small invertebrates in nature.
Native to coastal waters of Venezuela , Guyana , Suriname , French Guiana and northern Brazil .
notes: This mass-produced fish is adaptable and will do well in most tanks.
It does look particularly effective in a heavily-planted arrangement though, and can appear a little washed out in very spartan setups.

fi-hyphessobrycon-eques.title: Hyphessobrycon eques
fi-hyphessobrycon-eques.summary: The serpae tetra, Megalamphodus eques, is a characid with an enormous range through much of the Amazon drainage and the Río Paraguay. Very common in the trade, it is also sold as the 'jewel', 'red…
rows: group of at least 12 specimens should be considered the minimum requirement since this increases the likelihood that the fish will be distracted by each other rather than their tankmates but will result in a more effective, natural-looking display.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
notes: Choice of decor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with live plants and a dark substrate.
A natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots are formed.

fi-moenkhausia-sanctaefilomenae.title: Red-eye Tetra
fi-moenkhausia-sanctaefilomenae.summary: The red-eye tetra, Bario sanctaefilomenae, is a characin from Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina, living mostly in clear rivers that feed the Pantanal. All fish in the trade are captive-bred in huge…
notes: Quite an adaptable species that will thrive in most well maintained tanks, although it doesn't like very brightly lit or sparsely decorated environments.
It looks excellent in a densely planted tank.

fi-hyphessobrycon-flammeus.title: Flame Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-flammeus.summary: The flame tetra, Hyphessobrycon flammeus, is a small characid from Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo states in Brazil. Popular in the hobby, it is bred commercially in several countries and also sold as…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens since this species forms temporary dominance hierarchies within which males compete for female attention, and therefore displays more interesting behaviour and better colouration when maintained in numbers.
Omnivore. Omnivorous, feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, organic detritus, and suchlike in nature.
Restricted to the neighbouring states of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo in southwestern Brazil , although its current distribution is somewhat uncertain.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with live plants and a dark substrate.
A natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots are formed.
